caption: The drawing depicts a single hand tool, which appears to be a rake or similar implement, set against a plain, light-colored background. The rake is composed of a long, straight handle that is attached at a slight angle to a horizontal crossbar. The handle is drawn in a dark gray shade, and it tapers slightly as it extends upward, ending in a small, simple heart-shaped loop. This heart shape is formed by bending the metal of the handle. The crossbar supports seven evenly spaced, downward-facing tines, each of which is depicted as a thick, dark line with a curved hook at the end, giving a distinct hooked appearance. The tines are parallel to one another and perpendicular to the crossbar, and they are all drawn with a similar thickness and curvature. The entire tool is rendered in a monochromatic gray tone, suggesting a metallic material. The drawing itself is centered on the page with ample empty space around the object, and the composition is vertical, emphasizing the length of the handle. In the bottom right corner of the page, small printed text reads: "FRANCIS LAW. SWAHILI."
title: Toast Rack
